items.title: PCRS and NHS Wales primary care respiratory update, Cardiff, 20 October 2026
items.summary: PCRS is running a one-day essential primary care respiratory update in Cardiff on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with NHS Wales Performance and Improvement and members of the National Respiratory Audit Programme. A concentrated Welsh primary care respiratory audience.

items.title: GP who entered incorrect data in death certificates suspended for 10 months
items.summary: A GP who entered incorrect data while completing death certifications will be suspended for 10 months, a fitness-to-practise tribunal has ruled.

items.title: Government announces £33.2m to tackle infectious disease threats
items.summary: The Government has said it will invest £33.2m in eight projects to tackle overseas disease outbreaks that pose risks to the UK. It includes work on vaccines against Ebola, Plague, Marburg, Lassa fever, Nipah virus, chikungunya and Mayaro in low and middle-income countries where outbreaks are happening.

items.title: Dr Iain Morrison: ‘A GP career needs to be sustainable over decades’
items.summary: Pulse LIVE Glasgow saw Pulse editor Sofia Lind sit down with Scottish GPC chair Dr Iain Morrison to discuss increased funding, industrial action threats and how being a GP can again become a long-term career prospect A year ago, the Scottish Government ended the dispute with the BMA’s Scottish GP Committee by…

items.title: Key questions on coeliac disease
items.summary: Gastroenterology specialists Dr Mohamed Shiha and Professor David Sanders discuss key questions in the diagnosis and management of coeliac disease, including on serological testing, when biopsy is required, dietary and nutritional support and how to approach persistent symptoms despite a gluten-free diet.

items.title: ‘Same-day GP hubs’ to be established as part of ICB neighbourhood health plan
items.summary: One ICB has revealed more details about its plans for neighbourhood health, including transforming 12 community urgent treatment centres into nine ‘same-day GP hubs’.

items.title: Nurses asked to join baking fundraiser to support colleagues facing hardship
items.summary: Nurses, midwives and colleagues are being urged to participate in a national bake sale initiative in the hope of raising money to support those among the workforce facing financial hardship.

items.title: GPs should take on long-term ADHD management, landmark review recommends
items.summary: GPs should take on long-term management of ADHD under nationally-mandated shared care arrangements, the landmark Government review into ADHD and autism has recommended.

items.title: Nurse struck off after meds errors including giving a patient adrenaline instead of flu jab
items.summary: A community nurse has been struck off the register after giving a cancer patient adrenaline instead of a flu vaccination, as well as a series of other medication errors.

items.title: GP architect of neighbourhood health reforms to leave NHS England
items.summary: Dr Claire Fuller, the GP who led the landmark review of primary care that laid the foundations for neighbourhood health reforms, is leaving NHS England at the end of this month.

items.title: Top ten advice and guidance requests in urology
items.summary: Urology specialist registrar Dr Rebecca Smith, Consultant Urologist Dr Joe Jelski and GPSI in urology Dr Jonathan Rees describe the ten most typical advice and guidance requests in urology and how they should be managed 1.

items.title: UKHSA issues vaccination plea amid ‘possible signs’ of early flu season
items.summary: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has stressed the importance of vaccination uptake as latest data shows ‘possible signs’ of an early flu season. While still at ‘very low’ levels, flu activity throughout September has been higher than in the same period during the last four winter seasons.

items.title: Health officials urge vaccination amid signs of early flu season
items.summary: Health officials are urging people to get vaccinated amidst signs that the UK is facing an early flu season. Surveillance data from GPs and hospitals shows increased influenza activity and positivity rates largely being driven by young adults.

items.title: Unions submit 2027/28 pay claim for NHS nurses in Scotland
items.summary: A pay claim for nurses working in Scotland’s NHS has been sent to the Scottish Government by health unions – with a warning that negotiations must begin soon to avoid a delayed uplift for 2027/28.

items.title: Smoking rates halve as over one million never-smokers take up vaping
items.summary: The Government has hailed statistics showing fewer than one in 10 in England now smoke, while also condemning news that over one million who never smoked are now vaping.

items.title: Less than two weeks until Nursing in Practice’s virtual event on chronic conditions
items.summary: With less than two weeks to go until Nursing in Practice Virtual: Chronic Conditions, now is the time to secure your space.

items.title: Nurse-led youth vaping support service launched
items.summary: A nurse-led support service aimed at tackling smoking and vaping among young people has been launched in Derbyshire. The service – which has been described as a ‘first-of-its-kind’ and is named Vibe – will be run by a specialist community public health nurse across 10 secondary schools in the area.

items.title: GP-supervised physician associates seeing undifferentiated patients ‘dangerous’, BMA warns
items.summary: The BMA has criticised ‘dangerous’ Government proposals for physician associates (PAs) to treat undifferentiated patients in GP practices in some circumstances.

items.title: Independent review of Scotland’s maternity services begins
items.summary: An independent review of maternity services across Scotland has begun, examining how care can be improved for women, babies and families.

items.title: Government could miss treatment waiting time target due to GP referrals increase
items.summary: The Government is not on course to meet its referral-to-treatment target due to an increase in GP referrals, possibly linked to improved access to general practice, a leading health think tank has warned.

items.title: Skin lightening treatments and their risks: what nurses need to know
items.summary: Although skin lightening – also known as skin bleaching – is a controversial practice, people turn to it for a wide variety of reasons.

items.title: PA today, AP tomorrow
items.summary: The clairvoyant Copperfield on how advanced practitioners have become the new physician associates in general practice ‘I told you so’ blogs are so annoying that I’m going to say, while I did tell you so, I wish I hadn’t. We’re back to physician associates (PAs). Remember them?

items.title: New diabetes guidance, ADHD and polypharmacy on Pulse LIVE Liverpool agenda
items.summary: GPs can hear the latest on new NICE diabetes guidance, ADHD management and shared care, polypharmacy and the new chickenpox vaccination programme at Pulse LIVE Liverpool next month.

items.title: BMA keeping ‘robust’ industrial action plan for future, Scottish GPC chair tells Pulse LIVE
items.summary: Exclusive The BMA in Scotland prepared a ‘robust plan’ for GP industrial action which was used as leverage with the Government and which they will ‘keep just in case for the future’, the GPC chair has told Pulse LIVE.

items.title: iHV spotlights ‘lifesaving’ contributions made by health visitors
items.summary: The chief executive of the Institute of Health Visiting (iHV) has vowed to keep pushing for a ‘better future’ for babies, children and families – while spotlighting the ‘lifesaving’ contributions made by health visitors.

items.title: One million people who have never smoked now vaping, data reveals
items.summary: More than a million people who have never smoked are now vaping in Great Britain, new data has revealed.

items.title: PA review lead Professor Gillian Leng to head up GP indemnity provider
items.summary: The head of the review into the role of physician associates (PA) has been named the new president of the Medical Protection Society (MPS). Professor Gillian Leng takes over from Professor Dame Jane Dacre, who completed her eight-year tenure as MPS president in June 2026.

items.title: Oral weight loss medicine ads banned by watchdog
items.summary: The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) has ruled that adverts from two online pharmacies broke the rules by promoting oral GLP-1 weight loss medicines to the public. The rulings are the watchdog’s first involving oral GLP-1 weight loss medicines and concern ads from Simple Online Pharmacy and Pharmacy Online.

items.title: Every 20 Seconds: bringing the human story of kidney disease to the stage
items.summary: Advanced kidney care nurse Gloria Munoz-Figueroa describes how personal tragedy and the global toll of kidney disease inspired her to create the upcoming play Every 20 Seconds, and how she hopes the play can raise awareness, support kidney patients and spark conversations beyond the clinic.

items.title: Man charged with murder following death of Norfolk GP Dr Hannah Terry
items.summary: A man has been charged with murder following the death of a GP in Norfolk. Norfolk police confirmed that a man has been charged with murder following the death of a woman in Dersingham.

items.title: Final days to have say on protecting ‘nurse’ title
items.summary: Nurses have until tomorrow evening to have their say on protecting the title ‘nurse’ in law. Health minister Alison McGovern has urged the profession to make the most of this ‘crucial opportunity’ and inform the government’s call for evidence which closes at 11.59pm on Thursday 8 October.

items.title: Hepatitis A infections identified in Newcastle primary schools
items.summary: Two hepatitis A cases have been identified at primary schools in Newcastle, officials from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) have confirmed.

items.title: The top 10 triggers for complaints against GPs
items.summary: Dr Udvitha Nandasoma at the MDU shares the takeaways for GPs from an analysis into the most likely causes of complaints in general practice As a GP, you’ll receive many expressions of thanks throughout your career. But there will also be interactions that don’t go so well and cases where the patient makes a complaint.

items.title: Sharp rise in year-long community care waits for children
items.summary: More than one in four children on waiting lists for community health services in England have been waiting at least a year for treatment, according to new analysis by The King’s Fund. The think tank found that 86,000 children had been waiting for 52 weeks or longer in July 2026, accounting for 27% of those...

items.title: Murder investigation launched following death of ‘dedicated GP’
items.summary: A murder investigation has been launched following the death of a woman in Norfolk, who has been named locally as GP Dr Hannah Terry. Yesterday Norfolk Police said that detectives were granted extra time to question a man arrested following the death of a woman in Dersingham.

items.title: ‘We’re closing the gaps in palliative care through closer collaboration with GP practices’
items.summary: Marie Curie clinical lead for South West England Lucy Dowland explores how embedding healthcare professionals from the charity within GP practices has improved patient care and stopped individuals falling through the cracks.

items.title: CVD benefits of semaglutide not fully explained by weight loss
items.summary: The cardiovascular benefits of the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide cannot be fully explained by weight loss or improvements in other known risk factors, according to a new analysis of a major clinical trial.

items.title: Practice nurses invited to help test cervical screening system changes
items.summary: Practice nurses are being invited to take part in research to help shape changes to the Cervical Screening Management System (CSMS). NHS England is looking for nurses and administrative staff who work with CSMS prior notification or non-responder lists to test new screens and processes.

items.title: PAs can see ‘limited’ undifferentiated patients under GP supervision, says draft guidance
items.summary: Physician associates (PAs) working in GP practices can assess ‘limited groups of undifferentiated patients’ under heavy supervision from GPs, according to draft guidance produced by the Government.

items.title: Figures showing increased GP investment should be ‘treated with caution’, BMA warns
items.summary: New data has shown that investment in general practice in Northern Ireland has increased in real terms since the last financial year – but the BMA warned that the figures should be ‘treated with some caution’.

items.title: Call for hospice funding to ‘keep pace’ with NHS nurse pay rises
items.summary: Hospices require improved funding to help ‘safeguard the future’ of nurses working within the sector, a leading charity has urged. Hospice UK has reiterated its concerns about a lack of funding for staffing costs amid recent funds allocated by the government to help improve buildings and infrastructure.

items.title: Information for nurse prescribers on Levemir discontinuation issued
items.summary: A National Patient Safety Alert has been issued over the discontinuation of the diabetes drug Levemir in December. Stocks of Levemir (insulin detemir) FlexPen pre-filled pens and Penfill cartridges are expected to be exhausted by the end of the year.

items.title: Japanese encephalitis: prevention, vaccination and travel advice
items.summary: Japanese encephalitis is a mosquito-borne viral infection and an important cause of viral encephalitis in Asia and parts of the Western Pacific. Although the risk to most travellers is low, infection can result in severe neurological disease, long-term disability and death.

items.title: A guide to common childhood illnesses: threadworm
items.summary: Threadworm (enterobiasis) is the most common parasitic worm infection in the UK, particularly affecting primary school-aged children. Transmission occurs via the faecal–oral route following ingestion of microscopic eggs, which can survive on surfaces for up to 2 weeks.

items.title: Deprivation of liberty after the 2026 Supreme Court judgment
items.summary: The law relating to deprivation of liberty has changed significantly following a landmark UK Supreme Court judgment issued in June 2026.

items.title: The Nurse Roots pilot: a new approach to practice nurse student placements
items.summary: This article presents the development and evaluation of the Nurse Roots pilot, a hybrid placement model designed to expand access to high-quality general practice experiences for pre-registration nursing students.

items.title: Leaving no one behind: smoking cessation support for everyone who needs it
items.summary: Amid the widespread celebrations about the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026, it is important to remember that adults who smoke still need support to quit.

items.title: Cancer-related lymphoedema: an overview for general practice to support wider care
items.summary: Lymphoedema is a chronic condition that can be primary or secondary, the latter being the more common type. It often develops following treatment for cancer, and is particularly common in women who have undergone treatment for breast cancer. Early diagnosis and treatment are key to preventing progression.

items.title: Anti-racism principles and their application to nursing practice
items.summary: Irma Kock discusses the Nursing and Midwifery Council's anti-racism principles, including why they are needed, expectations for practitioners and their application to primary care nursing.

items.title: Protecting health, preventing inequality
items.summary: Practice Nursing, Volume 37, Issue 10, Page 369-369, October 2026.

items.title: Cancer-related lymphoedema: an overview for general practice to support wider care
items.summary: Lymphoedema is a chronic condition that can be primary or secondary, the latter being the more common type. It often develops following treatment for cancer, and is particularly common in women who have undergone treatment for breast cancer.

items.title: ICBs must use data and patient feedback to improve GP access, says Healthwatch
items.summary: ICBs should use access data and patient feedback to understand which patient groups face greater barriers when contacting their practice and ‘support practices to improve’, Healthwatch has recommended.

items.title: Ageing and declining GPN workforce a ‘key challenge’ in Scotland
items.summary: The Scottish Government’s professional nursing advisor for primary care, Claire Steven, sits down with Nursing in Practice editor Megan Ford at an exclusive conference in Glasgow to discuss the priorities, challenges and future hopes for general practice nursing.

items.title: School nurse workforce falls by almost 40% since 2010, analysis reveals
items.summary: The school nursing workforce has dropped by more than 1,100 professionals in England since 2010, according to a new analysis which has prompted fresh concerns around the preventative and early care that children are missing out on.

items.title: GP practices affected by NHSE list-cleansing to be offered support, says minister
items.summary: Exclusive The primary care minister has committed to ‘putting in place support where necessary’ for GP practices negatively affected by NHS England’s current list-cleansing drive.

items.title: ‘Would I be shinier if I left the NHS?’
items.summary: We received 100 excellent entries for our writing competition – our highest ever received – and we are now ready to announce our winner. Our judges said that Dr Shikha Banerjee’s piece was excellently written, articulated a feeling that many GPs will resonate with and was done so with humour and wit.

items.title: Physician associates’ union granted permission for judicial review over Leng recommendations
items.summary: A legal challenge over the Leng review recommendations can now proceed to a judicial review on some grounds, the High Court has decided.

items.title: Plans unveiled for a ‘public health approach’ to domestic abuse
items.summary: The government has outlined measures that will see violence against women and girls given a ‘public health approach’ – including new specialist support accessed via general practice.

items.title: Salaried GPs should be put on pay scale similar to consultants’, says BMA
items.summary: The BMA’s sessional GPs committee has called for equal career earnings between GPs and consultants to recognise their ‘equal status in the NHS’. The committee has adopted a policy calling for salaried GPs to be put on a pay scale similar to consultants’, rather than on a recommended pay range as they currently are.

items.title: MenB vaccination only taken up by a quarter of students heading for university
items.summary: Three-quarters of Year 13 students eligible for the meningitis B vaccine have not taken up the offer available through pharmacies, public health officials have warned.

items.title: Instilling vaccine confidence: the power of conversation
items.summary: At a recent Nursing in Practice virtual event, professional officer for the School and Public Health Nurses Association (SAPHNA), Susie Scales, explored a range of tools and techniques nurses can use when trying to help improve a patient’s confidence in vaccines.

items.title: Next year’s GP contract to be decided through consultation again, Government tells BMA
items.summary: Exclusive The Government has told the BMA that next year’s GP contract will again be decided through a consultation with several stakeholders – but there will be ‘bilateral talks’ with the union prior and alongside it.

items.title: NMC to ‘strengthen’ monitoring of nursing education
items.summary: The nursing regulator has vowed to take a more ‘proactive approach’ when monitoring the quality of nursing and midwifery training programmes.

items.title: NHSE hints at ‘potential contractual action’ around same-day urgent GP access target
items.summary: NHS England has said that there is ‘potential for contractual action’ against practices around its target for 90% of urgent patients to be seen on the same day.

items.title: Evidence is ‘reassuring’ for women who become pregnant while taking GLP-1 drugs
items.summary: Exposure to GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes drugs around conception does not appear to be linked to a detectable increase in adverse outcomes for mothers or babies, a large review of the evidence has concluded.

items.title: Safety alert issued for ‘dangerous’ baby sleeping bag products
items.summary: A safety alert has been issued for certain baby sleeping bags following concerns over the risk of overheating and suffocation. The Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) alert advises parents and carers not to buy – and to stop using – any sleeping bag products that lack armholes or which include a hood for...

items.title: NHS England commissions ‘external evaluation’ of advice and guidance
items.summary: NHS England has commissioned an ‘external evaluation’ of advice and guidance (A&G), which is expected to report its first findings before March next year.

items.title: What’s causing this pale macular rash affecting the chest and upper back?
items.summary: Speedy skins: Our latest quick quiz in dermatology asks – what could be the diagnosis in this patient who has developed a rash with pale macules affecting the chest, shoulders and upper back Note cases in this series are hypothetical and created for educational purposes Note AI was used to assist with development of…

items.title: Inability to book GP appointments online is causing ‘a lot of frustration’, says NHSE chair
items.summary: There is ‘a lot of frustration’ from patients about not being able to book a GP appointment online and NHS England must accelerate work around this, the commissioner’s chair has said.

items.title: Nurses alerted to ‘potentially harmful’ online ads for baby products
items.summary: Nurses have been urged to be aware of ‘potentially harmful claims’ being made in online advertisements promoting certain baby products.

items.title: Vomiting in infants: when is it reflux, and when should we worry?
items.summary: Dilemmas in paediatrics: GPwER in paediatrics Dr David Capehorn discusses how to assess the vomiting infant, and distinguish normal physiology, overfeeding and milk allergy from the rare scenarios where a child needs urgent referral Note cases discussed in this article are hypothetical and created for educational…

items.title: PCOS to PMOS name change among featured sessions at free Pulse virtual event
items.summary: GPs are invited to a free two-day virtual event in October, focussed on everyday presentations in primary care.

items.title: Health news watch: the male contraceptive pill, assisted dying bill and more
items.summary: Here, we look at the clinical news that patients might have read in the mainstream news media in September and provide the original evidence behind the stories so that you can answer any questions that may come up. Cahal McQuillan reports.

items.title: Cervical screening updates and breast cancer prevention to feature at Nursing in Practice North
items.summary: Updates to the cervical screening programme – including the rollout of HPV self-testing kits – and a focus on breast cancer prevention and early detection will feature at our Nursing in Practice North 2026 event next month.

items.title: Guideline on diabetes distress calls for routine emotional checks
items.summary: Healthcare professionals should routinely discuss the emotional impact of diabetes with patients, according to a clinical practice guideline developed by the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD).

items.title: Clinical quiz: managing UTI in women
items.summary: Women frequently present with symptoms of urinary tract infection (UTI) in primary care, but diagnosis and treatment are not always straightforward. Nurses need to recognise when symptoms support an empirical diagnosis, when urine testing is useful and when red flags suggest pyelonephritis or another cause.

items.title: Expanded health visiting support to be rolled out across 1,000 family hubs
items.summary: The government has announced plans to expand health visiting and midwifery support in family hubs across all local authorities by 2028.

items.title: GP reimbursement scheme expanded to locums and funding transfers
items.summary: The GP practice-level reimbursement scheme has been expanded today to include self-employed locums, and to allow practices to transfer any unused funding to any other practice.

items.title: MenB vaccination only taken up by a quarter of students heading for university
items.summary: Three-quarters of Year 13 students eligible for the meningitis B vaccine have not taken up the offer available through pharmacies, public health officials warn.

items.title: Infant feeding and mental health support to be rolled out across England by 2028
items.summary: A ‘Healthy Babies’ programme like what used to be provided in Sure Start centres will be rolled out to all local authorities by 2028, the Government has announced.

items.title: NMC fee increase comes into force
items.summary: An almost 20% increase to the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) registration fee comes into force from today (1 October). In a statement for Nursing in Practice, the NMC has set out what nurses, midwives and nursing associates can expect when it comes to their payments following the increase.

items.title: GPs to refer to new specialist services for domestic abuse support in 12 ICBs
items.summary: GPs will be able to refer people to ‘new specialist services’ for domestic abuse support in 12 ICB areas, the Government has announced. At the Labour Party Conference in Liverpool today, health secretary Yvette Cooper announced the rollout of the services would be backed by almost £50m.

items.title: NHS England’s GP list-cleansing drive targeting six to seven million patients
items.summary: Exclusive NHS England’s current GP list-cleansing drive is targeting six to seven million patients, new documents have revealed.

items.title: Government to create national pension scheme for social care nurses
items.summary: A new national pension scheme is to be created for nurses and colleagues working in the social care sector, the government has announced.

items.title: ‘How GPs are using AI as a clinical reasoning tool – rather than just a search function’
items.summary: Dr Kevin Fernando contemplates how GPs’ use of AI is changing in clinical practice, evaluating results from a query analysis carried out by Medscape Artificial intelligence (AI) is already changing the way we find information in our daily lives, but how are GPs really using it in clinical consultations?

items.title: Public more likely to trust health advice from GPs than any other source, survey finds
items.summary: The public are more likely to trust information and health advice from their GP than any other source, a new survey commissioned by the RCGP has found.

items.title: GPs call for ‘parachute payments’ as list cleansing puts practices at risk of ‘going under’
items.summary: GP leaders across London have asked for urgent ‘parachute payments’ for practices facing sudden income loss from NHS England’s ongoing aggressive list-cleansing exercise.

items.title: Moving vaccinations out of practices ‘frees up nurse time but adds workload complexity’
items.summary: Moving vaccinations out of Scottish GP practices has freed up nursing time but has increased the complexity of the profession’s workload, an analysis has found.

items.title: PCRS webinar on breathlessness and chronic cough in adults, 30 September
items.summary: PCRS emailed members on 14 August 2026 announcing a webinar, Breathlessness and chronic cough in adults: challenges currently being faced by primary care, on Wednesday 30 September 2026, 19:00 to 20:00. Date and time taken from the PCRS mailing; not yet confirmed on the public PCRS events listing.

items.title: Prime Minister issues apology to social care nurses for ‘being let down for so long’
items.summary: The Prime Minister has assured nurses and other professionals working in social care they are ‘not invisible’ to his government and has apologised for the way in which they have been ‘let down’ by politicians.

items.title: Proposed national care service ‘utterly essential’ to securing NHS future, says Burnham
items.summary: The Prime Minister has used his speech at the Labour Party conference to warn that a broken social care ‘will break the NHS too’.

items.title: ‘I’m not an anxious person, but general practice has pushed me to my limits’
items.summary: Dr Katie Musgrave opens up about the work-induced anxiety she has experienced in general practice, wondering if others are suffering in silence Has anybody else ever experienced that heart-sinking feeling when you’re due to go back to work after a holiday, and you just can’t face it?

items.title: ‘I wasn’t emotionally prepared for retiring from being a GP’
items.summary: Former GP Mary Coyne shares her experience of how the emotional impact of retiring caught her by surprise As I started to approach retirement, I began to wonder what it might look like. The standard definition of ‘leaving your job and stopping work’ was not to my liking.

items.title: GLP-1s and SGLT-2s may help slow kidney damage in diabetes, study shows
items.summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor drugs slow decline in kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes, but the benefits are only seen if they also have albuminuria, a large US ‘real-world’ study has reported.

items.title: BMA opposes Government plans for trusts to commission primary care
items.summary: The BMA has opposed plans for trusts to commission primary care as part of the neighbourhood health model.

items.title: New ‘workplace health system’ to prevent GP fit notes
items.summary: The Government is pushing ahead with its plan to create a ‘workplace health system’ to help people stay in work and prevent the need for GP fit notes.

items.title: NMC four-year midwifery strategy targets racism and safety
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) has set out a four-year strategy for midwifery regulation aimed at supporting safer maternity care, with equity and anti-racism among its listed priorities.

items.title: RCN president warns immigration reforms could destabilise social care
items.summary: Royal College of Nursing (RCN) president Bejoy Sebastian has renewed calls for the home secretary to scrap proposed immigration reforms for care workers, arguing they are incompatible with ambitions for a national care service and could further destabilise social care.

items.title: AP concerns ‘similar’ to those around physician associates, says BMA
items.summary: The BMA has demanded an ‘urgent review’ is launched by the Government into the scopes of practice for advanced practitioners.

items.title: Nurses caught ‘snooping’ on patient records will be suspended immediately, warns NHSE
items.summary: Nurses and health professionals suspected of accessing patient records ‘improperly and unlawfully’ will be suspended immediately, NHS England (NHSE) has warned.
